entities.summary: The Sydney Mint in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, is the oldest surviving public building in the Sydney central business district. Built between 1811 and 1816 as the southern wing of the Sydney Hospital, it was then known as the Rum Hospital. In 1854 a mint was established on the site with the hospital building used to house mint staff as well as providing a residence for the Deputy Mint Master. A coining factory was built at the rear. Both of these structures have exceptional heritage significance and have been associated with major events in the colonial history of New South Wales. Sydney Mint is a museum in Oceania. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Sydney Mint played a crucial role in the colonial history of New South Wales, serving as a key institution for coinage and currency management from 1854 to 1861. Its establishment had significant economic implications, shaping the financial infrastructure of the region.
